thread:
incident-bot: paging: high 5xx and tokenization errors from canary after deploy of release/optimize-3.2.0 (commit 9f7b3c). See runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/canary-fail. Stats: error rate spike ~12% in eu-west-1, traces show TokenizerService returning 502 for chunked inputs.
Alex: ack — oncall here, joining. Can someone paste the canary percentage and exact change that went out?
Jamie: pushed a small change that added an experimental header-based router for tokenizer selection. Canary was 15% in eu-west-1 and 5% globally. diff: small routing switch; no model change.
Priya: looking at dashboards — latency + error spike started ~2m after canary. Affected paths: /v1/generate (text) and /v1/embed for long inputs. Error samples show "invalid segment length" from tokenizer binary.
Leah: Support flagged a Partner corp ticket: "we're seeing large numbers of failed responses and retries causing timeouts" — Customer impact: partial degradation, retries causing client timeouts. Raising severity to S2.
Carlos: if it's routing to an incompatible tokenizer variant, we can either flip back the router or revert the commit. I can issue an emergency feature-flag flip if we have a flag for the header router.
Alex: is there an existing feature flag? Where is it stored?
Jamie: yes, flag name is routing.tokenizer_header_enabled. It was rolled out with rollout=15% for eu-west. You can toggle via internal flag service: `flagctl set routing.tokenizer_header_enabled false --env prod`
Sasha: I'm running `flagctl` now and will follow up. If that doesn't clear, we'll revert the single commit.
Sasha: ran `flagctl set routing.tokenizer_header_enabled false --env prod` — response: OK. Rolling out.
incident-bot: flag change detected by policy watcher: routing.tokenizer_header_enabled -> false (initiated by Sasha). Canary scope: eu-west-1.
Priya: metrics: error rate halved within 45s in eu-west-1, traces show fewer 502s; overall system errors dropping. Looks promising.
Leah: Customer update recommended: brief note that we're rolling back a routing change and monitoring. I'll draft and ping for approval.
Carlos: while flag flip is in progress, I prepared a quick revert patch if needed. Revert command: ```git revert 9f7b3c --no-ff && git push origin HEAD:hotfix/tokenizer-revert && gh pr create --title "hotfix: revert tokenizer routing" --body "revert experimental router"```
Alex: good. Sasha — if the flag flip doesn't fully resolve in 3m, please run the revert flow and trigger deploy-bot.
Sasha: will do. Monitoring traces and p95 latency.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: hotfix/tokenizer-revert by Sasha -> staging -> canary eu-west-1 (15%) pending approval.
Jamie: note: the router introduced a fallback path that doesn't handle chunked token boundaries correctly. That explains long-input errors. We'll add more unit tests for chunk handling after stabilization.
Sasha: canary verification shows canary passing after flag flip; no new 502s for 5 consecutive minutes. Rolling back the canary is currently unnecessary.
Priya: still watching, but baseline restored to pre-deploy levels. No error spike in us-east-1.
Leah: sent customer message: "We've identified a routing change that affected a subset of requests in eu-west and have rolled back the change; services are recovering. We'll follow up with a postmortem." Customer replied with thanks, asking for ETA on root cause writeup.
Alex: thanks all. I'm handing this to the next on-call for overnight monitoring. Next on-call: Jamie, can you pick up the post-incident follow-up? Please coordinate the revert PR if any regresses.
Jamie: picking up. I'll own the postmortem and patching plan. I'll also add tests and a canary failure gate for tokenizer-related routing.
Carlos: quick action items: (1) add chunk-boundary unit tests (2) gated rollback in canary pipeline (3) add alert for tokenizer 5xx > 1% sustained for 2m.
Sasha: adding notes to the incident thread and moving metrics dashboard to 1min granularity.
incident-bot: incident handoff: incident responder Alex -> Jamie (on-call). Handoff timestamp 3654322200.
Alex: leaving now. Good work. :thumbsup:
Leah: filing a customer-facing timeline and linking to support ticket.
Jamie: I'll open the postmortem doc and invite folks. Expect draft in 24h.
deploy-bot: canary rollback not required; no deploy executed.
Sasha: closing monitoring loop for now, will escalate if spikes reoccur.
incident-bot: incident resolved (mitigated) — status: monitoring. Resolver: Sasha. Root cause: experimental header router mishandling chunked token boundaries. Next steps: prestage tests, revert PR ready if needed, alert tuning.
